prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1323; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Evidence goes against the account: a nearby camera shows no collision at that place and time.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a rear-end collision involving the insured vehicle and a claimant vehicle. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy and confirmed the driver at the time of loss is named on the policy. Police report and two independent witnesses place the claimant inside the vehicle at the reported location.

Entry 3: Photos of both vehicles show damage that is mostly consistent with the described impact speed and direction. The claimant's shoulder injury fits the kind and force of a rear impact of this type. No prior injury to the same body area is on record.

Entry 4: Counsel's office provided the medical file, which shows a usual course of treatment that tapered off as the claimant improved. The claimant has given the same account of the collision in every conversation so far.

Entry 5: A nearby traffic camera shows no collision at the stated place and time, which conflicts with the claimant's account. A neighbor also believes the claimant's vehicle was already damaged a few weeks before the claimed date. No prior damage to the vehicle is on record, but this needs follow-up.

Entry 6: Referred the file to the special investigations unit to resolve the camera footage conflict and the neighbor's statement. Reserves held pending review, and counsel notified that liability and the injury claim remain under investigation.
